videos.title: Is dementia a normal part of getting older?
videos.instagram:
Is dementia a normal part of getting older? No.

In Australia, an estimated 446,500 people are living with dementia. More than 100 conditions can cause it, including Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia and Lewy body dementia. It is much more common over 65, but it can affect anyone (Dementia Australia).

We built MemoryCare for people living with dementia and the people who care for them: reminders, medicines and help on one calm, easy-to-read screen.

Join the waitlist: https://getmemorycare.app/ (link in bio)

MemoryCare is not a medical device.

videos.title: Early signs of dementia
videos.instagram:
Early signs of dementia worth checking: memory loss, trouble with familiar tasks, confusion about time and place, and changes in personality (Dementia Australia).

If you notice these changes in yourself or someone close to you, talk to a GP. Getting help early gives more options. The National Dementia Helpline is free and open 24/7: 1800 100 500.

MemoryCare doesn't diagnose anything. It supports the days that follow, with reminders read aloud and one thing to do at a time.

Join the waitlist: https://getmemorycare.app/ (link in bio)

MemoryCare is not a medical device.

videos.title: How to talk to someone living with dementia
videos.instagram:
Four simple tips for talking with someone living with dementia: stay calm and keep sentences short, give them plenty of time, use names and relationships, and offer yes or no questions or a few choices (Dementia Australia).

We built MemoryCare the same way: large text, plain words and one thing to do at a time.

Join the waitlist: https://getmemorycare.app/ (link in bio)

MemoryCare is not a medical device.

videos.title: Why routines help in dementia
videos.instagram:
Why routines help: Dementia Australia advises maintaining routines to reduce confusion, and having all family and carers use the same approach.

MemoryCare reads tasks and medicines aloud at the right time, with one big button to mark each one done. Family set it all up from their own phone.

videos.title: For carers: you matter too
videos.instagram:
About 1.7 million people in Australia are involved in caring for someone with dementia (Dementia Australia). Worldwide, family and friends provide about 5 hours of care and supervision a day on average, and women provide 70% of care hours (World Health Organization).

Take time out, use support services and ask for help. The National Dementia Helpline is free: 1800 100 500.

With MemoryCare, family can see how the day is going without having to ring and ask.

Join the waitlist: https://getmemorycare.app/ (link in bio)

MemoryCare is not a medical device.

videos.title: Good days and bad days in dementia
videos.instagram:
Symptoms of dementia can vary through the day and tend to worsen over time. But sudden changes, such as new confusion about where they are, hallucinations or a big mood shift, can signal delirium, which is a medical emergency. Get help. In an emergency, call 000 (UNSW).

MemoryCare asks how they are doing once a day: Great, Okay or Not good. A note can be added and shared with caregivers, so changes are easier to notice. It does not replace medical care.

Join the waitlist: https://getmemorycare.app/ (link in bio)

MemoryCare is not a medical device.
